paper_metadata.title: Development of Ion-Plasma Coatings for Protecting Intermetallic Refractory Alloys VKNA-1V and VKNA-25 in the Temperature Range of 1200 – 1250°C

evidence.quote: Russian intermetallic castable alloys VKNA-1V , VKNA-4U, VKNA-25, VIN-3, etc. pos - sess a satisfactory combination of mechanical properties at up to 1200°C in 1000-h tests.

evidence.quote: Figure 2 d presents the microstructure of the VSDP-41 + VSDP-16 coating after a 300-h hold at 1200°C.
The coatings were deposited with the help of a MAP-2 commercial ion-plasma device by the standard method with successive deposition of a layer of nickel alloy with a thickness of 80 – 85 /c109m
and then a layer of an aluminum alloy to obtain a specific gain in the weight of 60 – 65 g /c47m 2 on the coated surface
The final formation of multilayer ion-plasma coatings occurred in the process of vacuum heat treatment at a temperature of 1050°C with a hold fo r 3 h [3, 4].

The presence of such inclusions lowers the heat resistance of the coating above 1100°C
Introduction of hafnium into alloys of the Ni – Cr – Al – Y sys - tem (VSDP-41) or replacement of yttrium with hafnium (VSDP-4) also increases the high-temperature strength of the coatings.
Alloying of the coating with a low amount of tantalum and rhenium (VSDP-3, VSDP-41) lowers the intensity of the processes of diffusion interaction with the protected alloy

The external layer of the VSDP-4 + VSDP-16 coating has a double-phase (/c98+ /c103/c162)-structure; the VSDP-41 + VSDP-16 coating is repre - sented by a /c98-phase and an inconsiderable fraction of other inclusions.
